title: Evaluate, break and repair the version you will deliver
promise: Complete a verifiable project milestone and keep evidence that another person can inspect.
why: A working demo is only the start. The handoff requires evidence about data, permissions, failure recovery and usefulness in the actual task.

theory.title: Set criteria before testing
theory.text: Write five project-specific acceptance criteria and identify release blockers. Use observable outcomes rather than “works well”.
theory.example: Criteria, thresholds and tested version saved before observing results.

theory.title: Run five test families
theory.text: Test normal input, invalid input, duplicates, unavailable service and recovery. Record input, expectation, observation and destination effect for each in My project.
theory.example: Five complete records; replaying an event does not duplicate its business effect.

theory.title: Repair and rerun the suite
theory.text: Choose an observed failure, explain its cause, make one small change and rerun every case. Keep before and after evidence.
theory.example: A repair with cause, change and regression evidence; if no failures occurred, introduce one deliberately in the test copy.

theory.title: Get a review
theory.text: Give another person the version and outcomes. Ask them to check at least duplicate handling and shutdown. Record feedback and required changes without inventing approval.
theory.example: Attributed review and visible pending issues; a self-check is not instructor certification.

errors.means: The result cannot yet be checked.
errors.fix: Run the case and save the observation; leave it pending if blocked.

canDo: Help draft test cases and explain observed errors
cantDo: Certify tests that nobody ran or approve on behalf of another person
